stages.headline: Height of an object: from distance d measure the angle α to the top; the right triangle gives h = d · tg α.
stages.headlineEnglish: Height of an object: from distance d measure the angle α to the top; the right triangle gives h = d · tg α.

stages.headline: Example: 50 m from a tower its top is seen at 30°: h = 50 · tg 30° = 50/√3 ≈ 28.9 m.
stages.headlineEnglish: Example: 50 m from a tower its top is seen at 30°: h = 50 · tg 30° = 50/√3 ≈ 28.9 m.

stages.headline: Distance to an unreachable point: measure AB = 60 m and angles A = 75°, B = 45°; then C = 60° and AC = AB sin B / sin C = 20√6 ≈ 49 m.
stages.headlineEnglish: Distance to an unreachable point: measure AB = 60 m and angles A = 75°, B = 45°; then C = 60° and AC = AB sin B / sin C = 20√6 ≈ 49 m.
